title: Quiet-flux anchors show a lower fitted 3.75 GHz activity response in Cycle 25
abstract: We compare Japanese 2, 3.75 and 9.4 GHz flux with Canadian F10.7 in quiet and rising parts of Cycles 24 and 25. Common-day monthly data give 62 early and 45 late months. At fixed F10.7 of 70 sfu, the fitted 3.75 GHz change is +0.23 sfu. At 140 sfu it is -5.98 sfu. The activity increment falls by 9.64% (six-month case-block 95% interval 5.12 to 12.67% lower). Normalizing the increment by quiet flux gives a 9.90% fall. Thus neither a constant offset nor a constant gain in that band explains both levels in the main fit. The 2 GHz increment change is +2.42% (-2.12 to +10.30). A shape test that removes gain and offset gives no clear change in any band. Twelve-month blocks include no change in the 3.75 GHz increment. These results separate background and activity response without a sunspot or Mg II reference, but do not identify a solar cause or reject affine calibration error. A 2017-2019 gap prevents a local test of the 2 GHz receiver change. We supply code, aggregate estimates, figures, source hashes and external-data retrieval instructions. External observations remain outside the bundle.

display.caption: Cycle 25 changes in fitted total flux at two F10.7 levels and in the difference between these levels. Intervals use paired six-month case blocks and omit instrument scale uncertainty. Twelve-month intervals include no change in the 3.75 GHz increment.
